purpose: One bounded derivation to test whether Poisson/dispersion in h=pr-qs preserves useful adjacent-gap structure. This card does not assert a cancellation theorem.

parent.needed_component: the signed four-distinct contribution over the full interval L<=t<=2B

exact_object.weights: the normalized nonnegative adjacent-gap hat weights after deleting both endpoint shares of every physical gap greater than Y^(161/1000)
exact_object.sum: 4 integral psi(t/B) sum_{p<r,q<s,disjoint} lambda_p lambda_r lambda_q lambda_s exp(it log(pr/qs)) dt
exact_object.top_resolution: |h| is naturally Y^(16/33+o(1)) when t is Y^(50/33)
exact_object.quantifiers: every sufficiently large admissible Y; the actual fixed selector, not arbitrary coefficients

desired_derivation.success_form: An exact or controllably approximated dual formula in which the zero mode cancels against the smooth semiprime main term and every nonzero mode retains a transform or correlation of the actual gap selector.
desired_derivation.usefulness: A nontrivial selector-sensitive dual norm would define a smaller theorem than GCG4 and justify continued analytic work.
desired_derivation.does_not_itself_prove: GCG4 unless the resulting nonzero modes have total size at most Y^(-1187/13000+o(1)).

stop_conditions: The first Cauchy or completion step replaces the four gap weights by arbitrary bounded coefficients.
The determinant-offset sum is replaced by an absolute close-pair count.
Poisson completion costs a full modulus q asymptotic to Y without a compensating selector transform.
The proposed zero mode is not exactly matched to the smooth main term.
The derivation silently assumes independence of consecutive-prime gaps.

licensed_falsifiers.abstract: Arbitrary coefficient subsets phase-align, so a selector-blind dual theorem is false or too weak.
licensed_falsifiers.fejer: Positive smoothing leaves the generic conductor tube and cannot provide the signed cancellation.
licensed_falsifiers.prime_density_pseudonodes: Odd-half-grid pseudo-primes pass coarse gap/density tests and still create an antipodal peak.
licensed_falsifiers.finite: The frozen vectors show a small four-distinct residual but are twin-edge-only and therefore cannot validate the dual asymptotics.

decision_rule.continue: Only if the derivation exposes a named selector-sensitive transform with a plausible published or provable norm estimate.
decision_rule.stop: If any stop condition occurs, record the precise first loss and demote determinant dispersion rather than iterating equivalent Cauchy/completion variants.
